explanations.text:
The skill is the one door into the shape catalog. Everything else only reads the folder.

  you: "the abstraction did not explain enough — here is what it should have looked like"
       a sketch, a photo, a marked screen, a rewrite; the run starts from
       that picture, not from a rule                                     ([the input](The input))
       claude weighs it against every shape's rules and example, and one
       decision comes out: a new shape, a changed rule, or a changed
       example — the smallest change that would have produced the ideal
                                                                   ([the comparison](The comparison))
       claude shows the decision and the exact new text, and writes nothing
  you: "yes"
       the folder changes on your word only, and the shape file records
       which project validated it                                ([the validation](The validation))
       without the word, the catalog stays as it was

  you: "the project telling was the one that fell short"
       the same door: a shape for the text of human/project.json — the one
       that pins files and their entries in place of blocks — enters from a
       validated instance, as one more file of the folder that says it fits
       the project                                                          ([the door](shapes))

Why: each validated change moves the decompiler and the compiler nearer
the perfect abstraction                                                      ([the aim](Why))

A human skill that creates shapes for the human compiler. puts it into [compiler/shapes/](e1:the door).

It's invoked when an abstraction shape didn't sufficiently explain. And it required [input](e1:the input) on what would an ideal shape would've looked. Each shape comes with rules and a general example so it's easier to understand when to use.

The input [compares](e1:the comparison) to the current shapes on the folder, its rules and the example and takes a [decision](e1:the validation) on whether to add a new shape. add or modify rules or modify the example. So the next time the decompiler or compiler has to use a shape it manages to get closer to the [perfect abstraction](e1:the aim).
